title: perf(canary): improve auto-detection for latency/throughput regressions and tighten rollout guards
author: Marcus Li
description: Summary: Tighten and extend the performance canary auto-detection logic to reduce false positives during normal workload churn, add adaptive hysteresis and KV-cache-aware signals, and wire stronger rollout guards that automatically pause or rollback canaries on sustained regressions. Motivation: Recent incidents showed noisy transient spikes caused canary automation to trigger rollouts unnecessarily; this change reduces risk while preserving fast detection of real regressions. What changed: 1) Detector: implemented adaptive hysteresis that adjusts sensitivity based on short-term variance and traffic volume; 2) Signal set: added separate latency/throughput windows, upstream queue depth and KV cache hit-rate as first-class signals; 3) Decision engine: introduce severity scoring and sustained-window checks (e.g., 5m sustained deviation before auto-pause) and allow configurable jitter tolerance per customer tier; 4) Rollout guards: add automated pause + notify path that escalates to a canary fallback when severity > threshold, plus a manual override UI flag; 5) Telemetry: new metrics and traces for detector decisions and guard actions; 6) Tests: unit + integration + a new perf-canary canary e2e to simulate traffic regressions. Checklist: [x] detector algorithm implemented, [x] unit tests, [x] integration tests, [x] e2e canary validation, [x] docs and console flags, [x] Linear ticket(s) linked. Risk & rollback: default thresholds are conservative; feature behind feature-flag canary.autodetect.v2 and rollout can be reverted by disabling the flag or reverting the service config. Deploy plan: staged rollout to canary fleet for 72h with close monitoring of perf-canary-alerts and the new detector.metrics.* dashboards. See related: ENG-1357, ENG-1382.
